elements.program: #11 App. A item 4: 'Dark matter is conjugate matter — alive, P.R.'s core conjecture: as χ particles (x-clumping, gated self-force) or … as conjugate monopoles localized in momentum'. §8 (plain passage): 'Dark matter, here, is ordinary matter's mirror-polarized cousin'. §4 P4: 'Matter comes in x-polarized (Standard Model) and p-polarized (χ) representations'. First written in the lab notebook, v0.1, September 2026 (its P4: 'p-polarized fields (χ, conjugate matter)').
elements.school: A proposal or candidacy, never derived, in eight papers before the notebook by the record's count. Minic, arXiv:2003.00318 (posted 2020-02-29) §6.2: 'The proposal here is that the dual sector (as already indicated in the previous section) should be interpreted as the dark matter sector'; §5: '(that could be interpreted as dark matter Lagrangian'. Berglund, Hübsch, Minić, arXiv:2010.15610 (2020-10-29), abstract: 'dark matter, on the other hand, comes from the degrees of freedom dual to the visible matter'. Edmonds, Minic, Takeuchi, arXiv:2109.12763 §4: 'Thus the entire SM would have a dual SM (which we propose, describes the dark matter sector)'. Berglund, Hübsch, Minic, arXiv:2212.06086 §6.4: 'the dual particles are conjugate to the Standard Model particles in analogy with the canonical fact that momenta p are conjugate to coordinates q'. Hübsch, Minic, arXiv:2604.19418 (2026-04-21) §5.1: 'every Standard Model particle has a dual fuzzy counterpart'. All lit.py FOUND. First public: Minic's Belgrade slides, 9 Sep 2019, slide 5 (read by me from the image): 'each particle of the Standard Model has a "dual" particle … dual Standard Model (hidden sector?)'.
elements.note: Case for overlap: the school states C1's sentence itself, one dual for every Standard Model particle and the duals as dark matter, and one of its reviews calls the dual particles 'conjugate' to ours as p is to q, the nearest published wording to 'conjugate matter' (in no record file). Against: every statement is a proposal ('could be interpreted', 'we propose', 'candidates'); the school alternates between the dual partner and the whole metaparticle as the dark quantum (Minic 2020's abstract, which flag 64 quotes, makes 'metaparticle quanta' the dark quanta, a claim the same group printed in 2017, arXiv:1709.04388 §5); and Minic 2020 §3 says its doubled formulation keeps 'the total number of degrees of freedom the same as in the purely electric formulation', which the paper does not reconcile with a separate dark Lagrangian. My verdict: same, for the identification as worded. Whether the school's 'dual' is C1's 'conjugate' is E2.

elements.element: E2 what conjugate or dual means
elements.program: #11 §3: 'Quantum kinematics is exactly invariant under ρ: (x,p) → (p,−x); the Fourier transform implements it unitarily'; 'any world with local physics must select a Lagrangian polarization'. §4 P2′: 'Only ω is rigid (symplectic rigidity ≡ constancy of ℏ)'; P4: χ in p-polarized representations. One phase space (x, p) at ℏ; χ is matter in its other polarization.
elements.school: Three senses. (i) Foundations: x̃ is momentum rescaled at ℏ: x ≡ q/a, x̃ ≡ p/b, ab = 2πℏ (Minic 2020 §3; arXiv:2109.12763 §2.2; LaTeX in the source, FOUND); FLM 2015 (arXiv:1502.08005 §2): 'Y can be thought of as a momentum coordinate'; FLM 2014 letter (arXiv:1307.7080): 'so we will refer to Y as coordinates in momentum space'. (ii) Where the dark sector is built (metastring, metaparticle): x̃ = x_L − x_R (arXiv:2407.06207 eq. 3.11) with [x,x̃] = iλ², [x,p] = iℏ = [x̃,p̃], [p,p̃] = 0 (§3.3); 'the canonically conjugate dual space, spanned by the difference of the left- and right-movers' (arXiv:1905.09463); the dark fields are backgrounds of p̃: 'Thus we have “dark matter” fields, φ̃(x), in the effective classical spacetime x description (after integrating over the dual spacetime x̃).' (2407.06207 §3.3). The school identifies (i) with (ii): the x̃ ≡ p/ε description 'will appear in what follows in the metastring formulation of string theory' (2407.06207 §3.2); x̃ is 'the dual (momentum-like) spacetime' (arXiv:2307.16712); 'dark' means 'the “dark” x̃-dependent fields' (2212.06086 §6.6). (iii) Field space: 'that target-space/field-space “canonical conjugateness” is induced from the domain-space canonical commutation relation between x and x̃' (2212.06086 §6.4). In the full zero-mode phase space x's canonical partner is p (arXiv:1706.03305 eq. 69); only on the reduced (x, x̃) space does 'x̃/{2πλ²} play the role of the variable conjugate to x' (§4.2). All FOUND.
elements.note: Case for overlap: in the school's own words its dark sector is the fields that depend on the 'momentum-like' coordinate, and that coordinate is the rescaled momentum of its modular foundations carried into the metastring; FLM call the (X, Y) units, with cell area ℏ, 'the natural metastring parameterization' and the length-and-radius reading of (x, x̃) 'deeply misleading'; in those units the commutator is iπℏ (r6 verifier's computation), so the 'string scale' contrast is partly a choice of units. On this reading the school's dark matter is matter on the momentum side, C1's placement. Against: wherever the dark fields are constructed, x̃ has its own conjugate p̃ with [p,p̃] = 0, a doubled phase space (bracket rank 4, executed by two agents), and the dark fields are p̃-backgrounds integrated over x̃ onto x; even the foundations' presentation (2109.12763 §2.2) takes the duals from p̃; the program polarizes one phase space with ω rigid at ℏ. My verdict: partial. The record's split ('matches C1 in their foundations; their model doubles phase space') is right in direction, but one of its citations ('canonically conjugate dual space') names the winding space, and it omits that the school identifies the two senses and adds a third, field-space conjugacy.

elements.program: #11 §4 P4: 'Matter comes in x-polarized (Standard Model) and p-polarized (χ) representations'. §11.4 (P.R.'s conjecture): 'momentum matter is similar to position matter, each electrically charged x-polarized particle having a magnetically charged p-polarized analog'; its separate-photon form gives the p-sector its own gauge field. App. A item 11: 'A full magnetic mirror-family, quarks included'. §12 names three candidates, not a dual Standard Model.
elements.school: A dual copy of the whole Standard Model, one partner per field: for every φ(x,x̃) 'there exists a dual' φ̃(x,x̃) (arXiv:2010.15610 §3); 'the entire SM would have a dual SM' (2109.12763 §4). Named partners: 'we should find a dual photon that is correlated to the visible photon, and that is distinct from the dark photon of effective field theory' (2010.15610 §5), dual gauge fields that 'have the usual Abelian gauge symmetries' (§4); a dual Z, dual QCD, a dual neutrino in a seesaw, a dual Higgs (possibly the inflaton), a dual axion (2212.06086 §6.4–§6.5; 2604.19418 §5.1, §7). Belgrade slide 5 (2019): dual photon, dual neutrino, dual quark. No dual charges. The prediction rests on a gauging the papers call ambiguous: 'There is a possible ambiguity in this gauging which depends on which configuration variables one decides to work with.' (Minic 2020 §5). All FOUND.
elements.note: Case for overlap: one dual per Standard Model field is §11.4's 'momentum matter is similar to position matter' and App. A item 11's full family; a separate dual photon with its own abelian gauge symmetry is §11.4's separate-photon form. Against: the school gives the duals no magnetic charge, or any charge; #11's χ form is not stated as a dual Standard Model; Minic 2020 §3's 'no overcounting' leaves unclear how many independent dark degrees of freedom there are (my reading). My verdict: partial: the one-partner-per-field structure and a separate dual photon are shared with §11.4; the magnetic charges that define §11.4 are not.

elements.program: #11 §4 P4: 'both couple universally to H; gauge forces do not cross polarizations', taken strictly: 'no kinetic mixing between the sectors beyond what gravity induces … ε ≲ 10⁻¹³'. §13 row 7: 'Permanent null (both dark-sector candidates SM-decoupled; P4 strict)', killed by 'Any confirmed non-gravitational DM–SM coupling'. Exception: §11.4's shared-photon form 'needs P4 restated'.
elements.school: Main line, beyond gravity: Minic 2020 §5, a Berry-phase-like term α′A_μ dÃ^μ/dt, 'uniquely different from the usual effective field theory interaction terms between visible and dark matter particles'; arXiv:2010.15610 abstract, 'the known Standard Model fields and their dark matter duals are dynamically correlated'; §4, mixing ∝ λ⁸/L¹⁰: 'This correlation becomes invisible in effective field theory, and it vanishes as either λ→0 or L→∞. Note that with a particular double scaling, this term can be finite!'; §5: 'The correlation is proportional to the fundamental length, and is finite even in the limit of zero momenta (deep infrared). Also, the usual visible photon/dark photon coupling is subdominant to this term that is inherent in our story.' Leading order: a sum on one metric (Minic 2020 eqs. 49–50); 'These fields are in general correlated, due to their non-commutativity. However, to first order in the fundamental length, we can treat them as independent' (2212.06086 §6.3). One prior paper, Hübsch–Minic arXiv:2407.06207 (2024-07-03) §5.3: 'The mass-scale of this correlation term defines the decoupling energy, below which the dark and visible matter interact as required, only gravitationally', M_SM ≈ 4.5×10¹⁴ GeV (4.484×10¹⁴ GeV recomputed by two verifiers); the same paper, §3.4: 'In general, visible and dark matter degrees of freedom are correlated (via the minimal length λ)', offered as the origin of a₀ ∼ cH/(2π). Strength never computed. All FOUND.
elements.note: Case for overlap: at leading order the school's sectors share only the metric; its non-gravitational terms are sub-leading and 'invisible in effective field theory'; and a prior school paper puts every energy below about 4.5×10¹⁴ GeV in a gravity-only regime, which is P4 strict wherever experiments reach. The program's own shared-photon form is not gravity-only either. On this reading 'their sector correlated with ours' draws a sharper contrast than the sources support. Against: the school presents the correlation as its distinctive prediction, finite in the deep infrared, dominant over ordinary kinetic mixing, seen at accelerators and in galaxies; the 2024 sentence cites BHM 2021 for the very term that BHM 2021 keeps in the deep infrared, and sits beside a λ-correlation offered in the same paper as the origin of a₀, unreconciled (my reading); BHM 2021 warns that λ⁸/L¹⁰ 'should not be naively considered to be trans-Planckian'. My verdict: different, for the school's main line; the school is not consistent, and the record should state the 2024 gravity-only sentence beside 'correlated'.

elements.program: #11 §13 row 7: 'Permanent null' in direct detection and at colliders; row 1: 'Knee at v* ~ 10² km/s; zero cluster signal (particle χ)'; row 8: our monopoles, a permanent null.
elements.school: Detection expected: 'dark matter quanta should be detectable through their particular metaparticle entanglement to visible matter' (Minic 2020 §5; 2109.12763 §4 'correlation/entanglement'); 'These type of correlations might be found in correlated events in the accelerators' (2010.15610 §5); the modified-dark-matter review: 'A more concrete theory for MDM quanta will allow us to test the whole scheme of MDM at colliders, dark matter direct detection experiments and indirect detection experiments.' (arXiv:1709.04388, conclusion); detection analyses 'should be revisited' (2212.06086 fn 32). The nulls, conditionally: 'If the quanta of modified dark matter are metaparticles, this may explain why, so far, dark matter detection experiments have failed to detect dark matter particles.' (Minic 2020 §5). Astrophysics: a₀ ∼ cH/(2π) called evidence for the dark–visible correlation (2407.06207 §3.4; 2604.19418 §5.1 'is evidence for'). No paper states a permanent null (code counts, 41 papers). All FOUND.
elements.note: Case for overlap: both explain the direct-detection nulls by the dual nature of the dark quanta, the school by metaparticle non-locality and the program by P4; the 2024 gravity-only regime implies no signal at accessible energies, as row 7 has; and the school's shape of argument, that a quantum's dual nature hides it from searches, is C3's for monopoles (my comparison). Against: the school expects detection through the correlation, at accelerators and in galaxy dynamics, plans direct-detection tests, and gives its explanation of the nulls only as a conditional. My verdict: different. The school's signals are non-gravitational DM–SM couplings, which row 7 names as its kill condition, so a confirmed signal of that kind would tell the two sectors apart; the a₀ correlation is a second candidate observable, which the program's record never discusses (no MOND, Milgrom or a₀ in #11, #1 or the note).

elements.program: #11 §8: 'χ propagates on g (equivalence principle; Bullet-Cluster-safe)'. §7: gravity in momentum space is a massive spin-2 field X; App. A item 10: 'Momentum space has its own gravity — vindicated, transformed: dynamical, massive, reciprocity-odd (§7)'. No account of G_N from a dual volume.
elements.school: After integrating over x̃, 'we get an effective theory of visible and dual (dark) matter in the observed spacetime x' (Minic 2020 §5, eq. 50), on one √−g(x) (also 2407.06207 §3.4). G_N and Λ from the dual space: 'the size of the above dual space is the gravitational constant' (arXiv:1905.09463, abstract); the x̃-integration 'defines the gravitational constant G_N' and produces 'a positive cosmological constant' (2407.06207 §3.4). 'a dual gravity sector (associated with a dynamical dual spacetime)' (2212.06086 §4.3). FKLM 2021 (arXiv:2104.00802): 'the metaparticle couples to the extended metric' (g on x, g⁻¹ on x̃). FLM 2013 (1307.7080): 'not only will space-time become curved, but momentum space as well'. All FOUND.
elements.note: Case for overlap: both make dark matter fall on the ordinary metric; both give the dual side its own gravity, and App. A item 10's 'momentum space has its own gravity' is FLM's 2013 sentence, which FLM trace to Born (1502.08005 §1); FKLM's extended metric, g on x and g⁻¹ on x̃, is #11 §5's H = diag(g, g⁻¹). Against: the school's dual gravity is a dual curvature that gives Λ and a dual volume that gives G_N; the program's is a massive, reciprocity-odd spin-2 field with no counterpart in the school; the program derives no G_N from a dual volume. My verdict: partial: the same for dark matter on g, different for what the dual-side gravity is.

elements.program: #11 §8: χ scatters with M(k,q) = 4πα̃m_χ/(q² + m_φ²)·F(k²/μ²), 'k the incoming relative momentum … with μ the χ quantum's intrinsic momentum-fiber width'; σ_T(v) = σ₀F(v²/v*²), a knee at v*, self-interaction 'strong in cold dwarf galaxies, off in hot clusters'. App. A item 3: clumping in momentum (open).
elements.school: No self-interaction specified: 'how does MDM self-interact?' (arXiv:1602.00055, an open question); dark matter treated as collisionless 'whether traditional or metaparticle' (2109.12763 §6.2). One force law, unpublished: a static metaparticle potential 'which is of the Friedel form' e^{−αr}/r^β cos(γr) (2212.06086 fn 31, credited to unpublished FKLM work; Belgrade slide 4 writes it as V(r, r̃), Yukawa in r − r̃, oscillating in r + r̃), with no velocity dependence. A wave form: 'Therefore, one could say that dark matter is fuzzy from the point of view of classical spacetime.' (2407.06207 §3.3). Zero hits for relative velocity, momentum-space locality, or localization in x̃ or momentum across 41 school papers (r9 code counts, reproduced). All FOUND.
elements.note: Case for overlap: the school's only inter-quantum potential depends on the separation r̃ in the dual coordinate as well as on r, and in its foundations x̃ is rescaled momentum, so an interaction shaped by separation on the momentum side exists in the school (my inference, weak); its fuzzy form sits beside the program's wave branch and X-condensate. Against: the potential has no dependence on relative velocity or momentum overlap, is unpublished and is never used as dark matter's self-interaction; there is no gate, knee at v* or cluster null, and the school treats its dark matter as collisionless. My verdict: absent-in-school for the χ form's dynamics; the fuzzy form is related to #11 §12's X-condensate, not to χ.

elements.program: #11 §12: 'Conjugate monopoles … magnetically charged topological solitons of the p-polarized sector, localized in momentum (§11, §11.4)', 'untested: p-localization open'. §11.4 (P.R.): each electrically charged x-polarized particle has 'a magnetically charged p-polarized analog'. App. A item 5: monopoles live in conjugate space, explaining non-detection.

Verbal parallels: Minic 2020 §3, 'In particular, the modular representation of quantum field theory introduces dual “electric” and “magnetic” variables', fields φ 'and their (“magnetic”) duals' φ̃, the same φ̃ that §3 derives from p̃, 'not only to the usual fields φ but also to their duals φ̃ (see section 5)', with 'no overcounting'; 2407.06207 fn 11: 'The dual spacetime x̃ is associated with conserved dual (magnetic) charges in the same context.' (gravitational corner symmetries); arXiv:2111.14205 (2021-11-28): Ẽ8 as 'the electro-magnetic dual' of E8, 'and they are physically indistinguishable'; FLM 2013: worldsheet dyons whose Dirac–Schwinger–Zwanziger quantization is the diffeomorphism constraint. All FOUND.
elements.note: Case for overlap: the school labels the duals that become its dark fields 'magnetic' and the visible fields 'electric', ties the dual spacetime to magnetic charges, and calls its dark heterotic factor the electric–magnetic dual: in words, the program's pairing of the momentum side with magnetic charge. Against: the labels name the variables of a chiral, duality-symmetric field formalism that adds no degrees of freedom; fn 11 concerns gravitational corner charges; the E8 pairing involves no charged matter; there are no monopoles, solitons or momentum localization. My verdict: absent-in-school. The parallels bear on the wording of §11.3–§11.4 and on flag 67, not on the monopole form; Minic 2020 §3's 'magnetic' duals and fn 11 are in no record file.

elements.element: E9 vacuum and the choice of polarization
elements.program: #11 §3: 'ρ is exact and spontaneously broken. The breaking is mandatory'; credits FLM with the preferred polarization: 'They treat the breaking as kinematical and call the choice "a dynamical question". This program's addition is to read it as spontaneous breaking, with η as the order parameter'. §4 P2′: 'η = HJ, with the real structure J chosen spontaneously'; refinement: ρ inside a continuous U(1), the polarization a Goldstone angle, a ρ-preserving potential needed. P5: 'The vacuum selects a polarization; ours is x-tilted; the mirror vacuum is equally lawful.'
elements.school: FLM 2013 (1307.7080, 2013-07-26): 'We call (η,J) a chiral structure on P, with generalized metric H=ηJ'; FLM 2014 (1405.3949) §2: 'The consistency of string theory requires J to be a chiral structure, that is, a real structure (J²=1) compatible with η', and 'This formulation does not require the presence of a bi-Lagrangian structure K. However when we look at solutions of string theory, we find this extra structure'; §1.3: 'the purely kinematical splitting of phase space into space and momentum space has to be made dynamical'. FLM 2016 (1606.01829 §2): 'The space U(d)/O(d) represents the choice of inequivalent lifts η that preserve the symplectic structure and the vacuum state'. FKLM 2021 (2104.00802): 'The symmetry breaking happens at the level of the vacuum sector, and thus a choice of ground state fixes a value of δ'; 'We now propose that the expansion of the Universe can act as a mechanism that selects the decoupling frame'; but 'In other words the dual Lorentz action is not a canonical transformation.' BHM 2022 (2212.06086 §4.3): O(1,d−1)₂ 'is effectively spontaneously broken' within fixed p̃. Equal availability: 'there is nothing special about the x^μ; we could have taken any linear subspace, such as x̃,p' (1812.10821 §2); 'we could have picked the dual, x̃,p polarization' (2212.06086 §4.4). FLM 2015 §1: in ordinary quantum mechanics 'this choice of polarization is immaterial'. No potential, order parameter or Goldstone mode in any school text (grep counts, all readers). All FOUND.
elements.note: Case for overlap: P2′'s formula and wording (η = HJ, J a real structure) are FLM's of 2013–14; the space of η-choices at fixed ω and vacuum, over which P2′'s order parameter ranges, is named U(d)/O(d) in 2016; a split absent from the action and present in solutions (2014) has the logical form of spontaneous breaking; a breaking tied to the choice of polarization is placed 'at the level of the vacuum sector', with a selection mechanism (2021), and the word 'spontaneously' is used for that group (2022); the other polarization is equally available (2018–22); a school-adjacent thesis speculates that breaking a modular U(1) 'may be used as a mechanism to fix the quantum configuration space' and would 'break the Born reciprocity in favor of the position variables' (Yargic 2021 §2.8, read by me in the PDF). So #11 §3's 'They treat the breaking as kinematical' understates the school, and 'selected by the vacuum' is not a clean difference. Against: the school's broken symmetry is the non-canonical dual Lorentz group, 'fundamentally broken at the quantum level' by λ, an explicit breaking, not an exact symmetry broken by a vacuum; FLM 2016 argue that a canonical change of polarization is not broken by choosing one; FLM call the choice immaterial in ordinary quantum mechanics where #11 makes it mandatory; there is no potential, order parameter, Goldstone angle or single vacuum for all matter, and another line of the school makes the polarization observer-dependent. My verdict: partial. The program's own addition is narrower than #11 §3 says: spontaneous breaking of an exact, ω-preserving ρ (inside its U(1)) by one vacuum, with η as order parameter, a ρ-preserving potential, the Goldstone angle and the K-sign lock.

elements.program: #11 §10: τ is hilltop quintessence on the Maslov circle, V = V₀[1 + cos(τ/f)], 'strictly w ≥ −1' (w: pressure over energy density; −1 for a cosmological constant), thawing wₐ ≈ −1.5(1 + w₀) (w₀ the value today, wₐ its rate of change); 'a·ã = 1 (ℏ does not run)'; dictionary 'Dual stiff ↦ Λ; dual Λ ↦ stiff; dual curvature ↦ negative dark radiation'. App. A item 9 (P.R.): 'Their collapse is our acceleration', open through dual stiff ↦ Λ; item 6: 'Conjugate universe shrinks as ours expands — promoted to theorem'.
elements.school: Dark energy from the dual side: 'the weakness of gravity is determined by the size of the canonically conjugate dual space, while the smallness of the cosmological constant is given by its curvature' (2010.15610 §2); w = −1 at leading order. Reciprocal scales: 'relate the dual spacetime volume to the observed spacetime volume as Ṽ∼V⁻¹' (1905.08269, 2019); x → ax, x̃ → a⁻¹x̃, 'In the limit of large expansion a→∞, the dual dimension shrinks to zero', and 'as the scale factor a_c gets larger the dual momentum becomes smaller' (2104.00802); 'in the early (small) universe the dual (“dark”) degrees of freedom dominate', de Sitter as 'a BCS-like entangled state between two CFTs', the past one 'in terms of dual degrees of freedom' (2212.06086 §4.3, §5.3). Equation of state: 'w_eff < −1' (2202.05266, 2022); Hur et al. (2503.20854, 2025): first model 'Clearly, w(a)<-1 for all a as anticipated', 'this model is clearly disfavored' by DESI DR2; second model 'w(a)≥−1 in all cases' with wₐ negative; §2: Λ 'does change with the volume of x' because x and x̃ do not commute. No contracting dual universe drives our acceleration (all readers' greps). All FOUND.
elements.note: Case for overlap: the school puts the source of our dark energy on the dual side, as App. A item 9 and #11 §10's 'kinetic energy in the dual frame' do; it ties the dual volume reciprocally to ours, App. A item 6's a·ã = 1 in form; its dual degrees of freedom dominate early and de Sitter is one entangled state of a dual and a visible description, close to App. A items 2 and 8; and its 2025 model has #11 §13 row 4's signature, w ≥ −1 with wₐ < 0. Against: in the school dual curvature is Λ, where #11's dictionary sends dual curvature to negative dark radiation and dual stiff contents to Λ; nothing contracts or collapses; its reciprocal relations come from a volume relation in Tseytlin's intensive action or a cell rescaling at λ², not from ω-rigidity at ℏ with one lapse; the school has published both signs of 1 + w; τ, the Maslov circle and the thawing corridor are absent (the 2025 fits lie at wₐ/(1 + w₀) = −3.0 to −3.8, r4's computation, reproduced by its verifier). My verdict: related.

propositions.id: P2 their sector correlated with ours
propositions.reason: 'Correlated' is the school's own word, and in its main line (Minic 2020; BHM 2021; EMT 2021; BHM 2023) it names non-gravitational terms: a Berry-phase-like term, bilinear mixing derived from the same λ² symplectic term that makes x and x̃ non-commute, a dual photon correlated with ours 'finite even in the limit of zero momenta' and dominating ordinary kinetic mixing, fermion mass mixing, and non-commuting visible and dual fields. As a difference from P4 strict it therefore holds against the main line. Qualifications the summary omits: at leading order the sectors are a sum on one metric ('to first order in the fundamental length, we can treat them as independent'); the strength is never computed; Hübsch and Minic 2024 §5.3, before the program, put all interaction below about 4.5×10¹⁴ GeV at gravity alone, while the same paper keeps a λ-correlation as the origin of a₀, so the school is not consistent; in two papers 'correlated' means only the observed modified-dark-matter regularity of mass profiles, which its authors allow may arise in ΛCDM. On the program's side, the shared-photon form of §11.4 is not gravity-only.

summary_line.verdict: Accurate in all three clauses, but it omits two qualifications. 'Its core is published (Minic and coauthors, 2020)' holds for print: the identification is a proposal in Minic 2020 §5–§6.2, posted 29 Feb 2020, after a public talk of 9 Sep 2019. 'Core' fits the identification in words, while the school's dual, where its dark sector is built, is a coordinate of a doubled phase space rather than the program's single phase space at ℏ. 'Their sector correlated with ours' uses the school's own word and holds for most of its papers, through terms beyond gravity of unstated strength. It omits that the sectors are independent at leading order, and that one prior paper (Hübsch and Minic 2024) puts all interaction below about 4.5×10¹⁴ GeV at gravity alone; the school is not consistent on this. 'Neither form was found' holds. On C1 the line understates how different the school's 'dual' is, and it makes the coupling contrast look cleaner than the sources are. The school's wider overlap with the program's setting (η = HJ, the choice of polarization, a breaking placed in the vacuum) belongs on other pages, not in this line.

dissent: (1) My case for overlap goes further than my verdicts in four places, and I do not adopt it there: the Friedel-type potential as an interaction on the momentum side (E7; it has no velocity dependence and is unpublished); the 'electric'/'magnetic' labels and HM 2024's footnote 11 as the magnetic mirror (E8; no charged matter); FKLM 2021's vacuum-sector breaking as the program's spontaneous selection (E9; the school's symmetry is non-canonical and broken explicitly by λ); and the 2024 gravity-only sentence as the school's position on coupling (E4; it is one sentence of one paper). (2) Against the r9 verifier on Q8: Minic 2020 §3 does tie its '(“magnetic”) duals' φ̃ to §5. It derives 'their duals φ̃ (see section 5)' from p̃ by minimal coupling, and §5 calls those duals dark matter (I re-read both passages). What the paper leaves unreconciled is §3's 'no overcounting' with §5's separate dark Lagrangian. So 'the paper does not say it' is too strong; 'the paper points to it without reconciling the degrees of freedom' is what I read. (3) Against the r9 verifier's record point 5 and the r3 reader: HM 2024 §5.3 does not make the school's sector the program's gravity-only sector at accessible energies. The same paper (§3.4) offers a dark–visible λ-correlation as the origin of a₀ in galaxies, and its April 2026 successor calls a₀ 'evidence for … the correlation of dual fields of fuzzy dark matter to the observed Standard Model fields' (2604.19418 §5.1). I therefore read the summary's 'correlated' as faithful but incomplete, not as understating the overlap in substance. (4) On E2 I lean further toward overlap than the record or the r1 and r2 readers. The school states that its metastring x̃ is the modular x̃ ≡ p/ε carried over (HM 2024 §3.2, eq. 3.5); its 'dark' fields are the x̃-dependent ones; and x̃ is 'momentum-like'. So the record's split between foundations and model is less clean than it reads. The doubling with an independent p̃ is real, so I keep 'partial'. (5) On the date I keep '2020' for 'published', against the r1 reader's proposal to move the priority to 9 Sep 2019: the talk is the first public statement, and the record's 'whose content is unknown' must change, but a talk is not a publication, and the verifier agrees that 'dated no later than its posting' holds for print. (6) On the brief's framing of clause 2: the program's own side is not perfectly clean either. #11's shared-photon form needs P4 restated, and P4 strict allows kinetic mixing induced by gravity (ε ≲ 10⁻¹³), so the contrast is main-line school against strict-P4 program, not correlated against clean. (7) Where I side with a verifier against its reader: r4's verifier is right that 'by construction' has a direct source (BHM 2021's derived mixing term); r5's verifier is right that the modified-dark-matter authors' preferred reading of their data goes beyond local effective field theory and is not gravity-only; and r6's verifier is right that FLM 2016 states the positive form of the compatibility statement. (8) The Yargic thesis passage, which bears on #11 §3's claim to the spontaneous reading, comes from outside the 45 school papers and was found only by the r8 verifier. I re-read its §2.8 in the PDF; an exact search missed one sentence because of a 'fi' ligature, and it was found after normalizing. I count it as a related, school-adjacent speculation. Files I wrote are in /home/paul/git/reinholdtsen/conjugate-matter/work/dual-sector/scratch/j-identity/: quotes.tsv, quotes2.tsv and their .verdicts (84 quotations, all FOUND, one loosely), numbers.py and numbers.out (day gaps and the 35-word count), pdfgrep.py, ran_v1.txt and yargic.txt (extracted PDF text).
